result:
None of the three solutions establishes the answer 1, so I cannot confirm any of them.

Solutions 1 and 2 correctly compute the stalk of \(\mathcal K\) at a diagonal point. The fiber \(b^{-1}(F,F)\) maps into \(\mathcal O_{w_0}\), where \(i^!\mathcal S\) is \(\mathbb Q[4]\), giving \(\mathcal K_{(F,F)}\cong\mathbb Q[-2]\). The step that fails is the extraction of the multiplicity of \(\mathcal D\):

- The stalk in total degree 2 does not force a \(\mathcal D\)-factor in perverse degree 5. In the perverse spectral sequence, terms in stalk degree \(-3\) can be cancelled by differentials from or to other stalk degrees, and other simple perverse sheaves can contribute to total degree 2 with stalk degrees \(\le -4\).
- A toy check shows the inference is invalid. If \(\mathcal S\) were the constant sheaf \(\mathbb Q_X[8]\), then \(\mathcal K\) would be the constant sheaf \(\mathbb Q_Z[-2]\), which has no \(\mathcal D\)-factor at all, so the multiplicity sum would be 0, even though its stalk at \(\mathcal F\) is also \(\mathbb Q[-2]\).
- The sign twist matters near the diagonal orbit \(\mathcal O_e\), where the solutions only analysed \(\mathcal O_{w_0}\). Also, \(\mathcal K\) is a Hecke-type convolution with \(j_{w_0!}\), which is not t-exact, so \(\mathcal D\) could appear in more than one perverse degree.
- Solution 1's description of the divisors by rank conditions is internally inconsistent, since \(Z\) has \(\operatorname{rk}A=1\), and Solution 3 is unsupported handwaving.

So the value 1 is not verified, and I believe the true value is likely different, though I have not computed it.

CHOICE: NONE
